title: First French Empire
capsule: The First French Empire was the continental state proclaimed on 18 May 1804, when the Senate conferred the imperial title on Napoleon Bonaparte, crowned Emperor of the French on 2 December 1804. Between 1805 and 1815 it directly annexed the Low Countries, parts of Italy and the German coast while its Grande Armée dominated a web of client kingdoms across Europe, before collapsing after Napoleon's 1814 abdication and briefly reviving during the 1815 Hundred Days. This metropolitan imperial state is distinct from its overseas colonial remnants, which had by then mostly fallen to Britain.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The surviving colonial territories of 1805–1815 are historically documented, but reconstructing precise territorial polygons for this rump empire is problematic given dispersed island holdings and contested occupation during the Napoleonic Wars.
